title: Behave: The Biology of Humans at Our Best and Worst

contents: The backwards clock: a behaviour occurs — then the explanation rewinds through one second before (neurons), seconds to minutes (sensory cues), hours to days (hormones), days to months (neuroplasticity), adolescence, childhood, the womb, genes, culture, and millennia of evolution
Us versus Them: the fastest, most consequential categorisation the brain makes
Morality: doing the right thing, once you've figured out what that is
Metaphor and symbol: the brain's confusion of the sacred and the visceral
Free will: the biology that leaves ever less room for it
War and peace: the conditions of our best and worst

audiences: Readers who want the full scientific machinery behind behaviour
Determined readers wanting the broader foundation it grew from
Students of neuroscience, psychology, and evolution
Anyone arguing about nature versus nurture who wants the real answer

sources.title: Reviews of Behave (aggregated)
sources.supports: The professional reception roster with documented verdicts: Wrangham in the NYT ('a quirky, opinionated and magisterial synthesis'), Barash in the WSJ ('one of the best nonfiction books I've ever read'), Poole in the Guardian ('a miraculous synthesis of scholarly domains'), plus Washington Post, Star Tribune, Kirkus, and PW raves.

sources.title: A Monumental, but Flawed, Effort to Understand Behavior
sources.supports: A physician-scientist's documented critique: fMRI/PET measure blood flow and are confounded by non-neural processes; the book does not grapple with the replication crisis or effect sizes; animal models over-generalised; specific factual disputes (substance P and depression, adult neurogenesis and the Rakic dispute); moral philosophy and law underweighted; verdict 'deficient — with an implicit point of view... many errors of fact and interpretation'.
sources.limitations: One reviewer, with his own strong views; the neurogenesis dispute remains genuinely unsettled.

sources.title: Review of Behave (as documented in the book's reception record)
sources.supports: The science-journal register of the praise: a fast-paced course from a master teacher, exceptional in scale, scope, detail, and writing.

sources.title: Behave: The Biology of Humans at Our Best and Worst
sources.supports: Large, unusually warm reader reception for an 800-page science book, with recurring notes on density, the demanding appendices, and the free-will chapter's divisiveness.
